**Group:** Zooplankton  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A ctenophore (comb jelly): a large, transparent, gelatinous zooplankter, typically ovoid to lobed, bearing meridional rows of ciliary comb plates (ctenes) that can catch the light in bands. Bodies are soft and often appear as a faint rounded blob with some internal structure. Key features: large gelatinous transparent body, comb-row bands, no hard skeleton.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **siphonophore** | Siphonophores are colonial cnidarians forming chain- or ribbon-like assemblages of repeated zooids; ctenophores are single ovoid/lobed gelatinous bodies with comb rows. |
| **larvacean** | Larvaceans are small tadpole-shaped tunicates, often within a mucous house; ctenophores are larger ovoid comb jellies. |
